resources.string: The BMI Calculator helps you quickly understand if your weight falls within a healthy range for your height. BMI (Body Mass Index) is a simple and widely used method to estimate weight categories and support better health awareness.
BMI is a numerical value calculated based on your weight and height. Healthcare professionals use it as a quick screening tool to identify potential weight-related health risks.

Formula:
BMI = weight (kg) ÷ (height in meters)²

Example:
If you weigh 70 kg and your height is 1.75 m
BMI = 70 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 22.9

Underweight: less than 18.5
Normal weight: 18.5 – 24.9
Overweight: 25 – 29.9
Obesity: 30 or higher

BMI provides a quick indication of whether your weight may increase the risk of conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, or high blood pressure. It is a useful starting point for understanding your overall health.

BMI does not measure body fat directly and does not take into account:

• Muscle mass
• Bone structure
• Body composition
• Age or gender differences
• Fitness level

For example, athletes with a lot of muscle mass may have a high BMI, even if they have a low body fat percentage.

Use BMI as a general guideline, not a medical diagnosis.

• Combine it with other indicators such as waist circumference, lifestyle, and activity level.
• Consult a healthcare professional for a full assessment.

BMI is a useful tool for gaining insight into your weight status but should always be viewed in the proper context. Your health is influenced by many more factors than just BMI.
